claims.text: Mostly a clinical diagnosis; mild withdrawal needs no routine testing unless it is not clearly better within 2 to 3 days.
claims.quote: Patients with mild symptoms do not require routine testing unless improvement is not marked within 2 to 3 days.
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Alcohol Toxicity and Withdrawal

claims.text: Labs for heavy drinkers: CBC, electrolytes including magnesium, liver tests with PT/PTT, ammonia and albumin.
claims.quote: complete blood count, electrolytes (including magnesium), liver tests (including coagulation profile [PT/PTT]), serum ammonia, and serum albumin are often recommended
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Alcohol Toxicity and Withdrawal

claims.text: CT and lumbar puncture may be needed when severe withdrawal could be CNS injury or infection.
claims.quote: In severe withdrawal and toxicity, symptoms may resemble those of central nervous system injury or infection. Because concomitant medical and surgical conditions can occur simultaneously with alcohol withdrawal, medical evaluation with CT and lumbar puncture may be needed.
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Alcohol Toxicity and Withdrawal

claims.text: Severity: score it with the CIWA-Ar scale.
claims.quote: A clinical assessment tool for severity of alcohol withdrawal is available. Clinical Calculators Alcohol Consumption Screening AUDIT Questionnaire Clinical Calculators CIWA-Ar Clinical Institute Withdrawal Assessment for Alcohol Scale
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Alcohol Toxicity and Withdrawal, Clinical Calculators
